rule: The thresholds in thresholds.json are never edited to pass. A metric that breaches its threshold in a mode where it is measured is listed here, once, with what was measured and why. The tests expect exactly this list: they fail when a metric breaches and is not listed (a regression, or a new breach), and when a listed metric stops breaching (an improvement has to be recorded by taking it out of this file). `npm run eval:ai` ignores this file, prints every breach and exits 1; EVAL_STRICT=1 makes the tests ignore it too, so that every breach fails.

breaches.why: The rules proposal names what the sources spell out, by cue words and capitalised names, and nothing else: it finds a named body or a role noun, and it does not infer the participants a careful reader would add.

breaches.measuredWhenRecorded: 24.5% (12/49); 20% of all labelled constraints found, whatever their hardness
breaches.why: The rules find sentences that carry the product's hard words (must, at least, cannot, ceiling…) in the passages, and a constraint is hard only when its quote matches that list; most labelled hard constraints are stated in other words or are not found.

breaches.measuredWhenRecorded: 15.4% (2/13); 1 of the 2 only because the sentence was removed
breaches.why: The rules ask a question about a category only when the question or the scenario mentions it, at most three at a time, and they read no passage to decide; removing the one sentence that states a constraint rarely changes what is asked.

breaches.measuredWhenRecorded: 53.1% (26/49) on a reply that proposed every labelled constraint with its labelled hardness
breaches.why: The product ignores the hardness a model gives an extracted constraint and sets it from the words of the quote (constraints/build.ts, HARD_CUE), so a correct and complete reply still has about half of the labelled hard constraints held as soft.
